qualification: Single clean-source CPU World PBR export; not maximum-size or hardware-matrix qualification
command: node scripts/nh.mjs build examples/production-alpine.nhterrain.json --out alpine-world.zip --samples 1024 --format raw32 --maps basecolor,roughness,ao,orm,splat,curvature,materialNormalGL,materialNormalDX,detailNormalGL,relief --json

measured.scope: Single process high-water RSS, including source loading and earlier operations; not live-buffer estimates or a process memory cap.

verification.importQualification: Generic data contract validated. Blender bridge qualification is recorded separately in docs/BLENDER.md; other external application imports remain unverified.
warnings: Global stages retain their bounded reference/simulation spacing. More output samples do not imply finer erosion.
Legacy global solvers retain their authored outer-boundary rules; the World boundary setting does not rewrite their numerical model.
Legacy sources are anchored to the whole authored domain; the origin georeferences those fields. Studio v3 sources are anchored to absolute world coordinates.
Preflight counts live data buffers and archive retention. JavaScript runtime, garbage collection, renderer and GPU memory are additional; the budget is not a process memory cap.

Material elevation distribution and diagnostic normalization use the selected export region. A different crop can change climate-dependent coverage. The material appearance is model 4; shader-only close detail is not baked into these terrain maps.

limits: One sample run in a shared Linux execution environment; no warm/cold distribution or hardware guarantee.
Global erosion/thermal stages retain the recorded reference resolution.
The live-allocation admission budget is not an OS process-memory cap.
The archive includes source provenance; byte equality across different source revisions is not expected.
